title: Queen Lila and the kingdom in one room
hookLine: a dead king, a grieving queen, and a whole world inside one room
carry: the world takes shape in the mind
tomorrow: a queen finds peace without leaving home. why does her husband laugh?
last: ONE FRIEND BRINGS THE OTHER THREE.

lines: A CHAIR, A COAT, A MUG.
A QUEEN WHO CAN'T LET GO.
cards: After someone dies, a room can change. A chair, a coat on a hook, a mug nobody else uses. Queen Lila sits in a room like that.
King Padma lies dead in the palace, and she can't let him go. Long before, she had prayed to the goddess Sarasvati and been promised that when he died, his spirit wouldn't leave the palace.
Now, in her grief, she calls on the goddess again and asks to see where he is. And the goddess shows her.

teach.b: He's right there, in the space of that very room. But for him, it isn't a room. Inside it, Padma is living another life as a king, with a city, a court and a kingdom around him.

teach.h: YEARS FOR HIM, MOMENTS FOR HER.
teach.b: Years are passing for him, while for Lila only a short while has gone by. The palace room and the whole kingdom take up the same small space. Vasistha tells Rama this story for the book's big idea.
The world that seems so solid, so fixed in size and time, is shaped by the mind, a little like a dream. That's one of this book's central teachings.
The word he leans on is chitta, the mind, the field where all of it appears. A moment for one person can be years for another.

teach.h: A SMALL ROOM CAN HOLD A WORLD.
teach.b: A small room can hold a world. Neither measure is the final one. Think back to Rama at court, sure that nothing was worth holding.
Vasistha doesn't argue with him about the world's prizes. He goes underneath them. If the world takes its shape in the mind, then the mind is where the work is done.
In this book, yoga isn't mainly about postures. It's the mind seeing how its own worlds are made.

how: The story of Lila is one of the Yoga Vasistha's best-known tales among its readers, and teachers use it to open the book's teaching that the world takes shape in the mind.

o: a book of poses for a strong and flexible body
a sage's stories showing the world takes shape in the mind
a royal history of the kings who ruled before Rama

games.q: who's who in Lila's story — tap the pairs.
p: the queen who grieves and asks
the king, living on inside one room
the mind, where the world appears

s: in the story, Padma's spirit has gone to a far-off heaven
he's in the space of the very room, living as a king.
far more time passes for Padma than for Lila
years for him, a short while for her.
yoga in the Yoga Vasistha is mainly about postures
here it's mainly about the mind seeing how its own worlds are made.

games.q: your grandfather says one childhood summer lasted forever. your little sister says this summer flew by. by the Lila story, who's measuring wrong?
o: neither; each mind sets its own measure.
your sister; a summer is the same for everyone.
your grandfather; old memories always stretch.
games.why: in the story, years pass for Padma while only a short while passes for Lila, in the same room. the world takes shape in the mind, and neither measure is the final one.

practice: Choose one small corner of the room you're in: a windowsill, a shelf, the edge of a desk. Look at it for the whole sit as if it held a whole world, and let your eyes find one more detail each time they settle.
When the mind wanders off, notice where it went, and come back to the corner.

wordCard.voice: The Yoga Vasistha: here, Lila's story, a whole kingdom inside one room, because the world takes shape in the mind.

orig.note: Sanskrit chitta: the mind, the field where the world appears.
